title: Nonarithmetic lattices in complex hyperbolic dimension at least four
statement: For which \(n\geq4\), if any, is there a nonarithmetic lattice in \(PU(n,1)\)? This is the modern unresolved part of the notebook\textquoteright s broader rank-one arithmeticity question.
status: As of 10 November 2026, open in the literature located. The 2023 paper explicitly states the question for \(n\geq4\), and the introduction of \citet{yu2026mirror}, first submitted 30 October 2026, still reports known examples only in dimensions two and three. No higher-dimensional solution was found.

title: A conceptual proof of the first Gelfand--Dickey Jacobi identity
statement: Explain and prove the Jacobi identity for the coefficient-linear Gelfand--Dickey Hamiltonian operator through a structural construction, rather than a direct binomial calculation.
status: Resolved by the formal Volterra-group/coadjoint construction: \citet[\S\S5--6]{lebedevmanin1979volterra}, received November 1978 and published 1979. The full proof was read; the object is the first Gelfand--Dickey bracket.

title: Local algebraization of Harish–Chandra categories
statement: For a real linear connected semisimple group and bounded central-support domain \(D\), construct an algebra finite over the center realizing \(\mathcal C_D\); near a regular infinitesimal character, realize it by an explicit nice analytic matrix order.
status: Solved in the stated scope by Bernstein, I. M. Gelfand and S. I. Gelfand, presented 9 January 1978 and published March 1978; the nice-algebra theorem requires a regular infinitesimal character and a sufficiently small neighborhood. As of 10 November 2026, no extension to arbitrary singular blocks is asserted here.

title: Finite-action Yang–Mills critical connections beyond instantons
statement: Classify smooth finite-action SU(2) Yang--Mills connections on Euclidean four-space up to gauge, equivalently critical connections on bundles over the round four-sphere after removable-singularity compactification.
status: As of 10 November 2026, ADHM-type data classify the self-dual or anti-self-dual minima, while nonminimal critical points also exist. The checked 2026 gap theorem controls an energy range and does not give a complete classification of all critical points.

title: Fixed-charge instanton classification and connectedness
statement: For each charge \(k\), describe all \(SU(2)\) instantons on \(S^4\) up to gauge and determine whether their moduli space is path-connected.
status: As of 10 November 2026, as of 10 November 2026, as of 10 November 2026, the finite-dimensional construction was announced in 1977 and published in 1978; path-connectedness for SU(2) was proved by Taubes in 1984. Dayaprema--Waldron (2026), Theorem 1.2 and section 3.3, provide a new proof and explain the extension to SU(r).

title: Selecting combinations with prescribed inner divisors
statement: For fixed inner \(\omega\) and a finite family in \(H^\infty\), find a constant-coefficient linear combination whose common inner divisor with \(\omega\) equals that of the whole family; determine the exceptional parameters for a one-parameter family.
status: Known before the talk: Sherman\textquotesingle s two-function lemma is printed with proof in Sz.-Nagy (1976), and the same paper proves a simultaneous countable-row extension with summable coefficients. As of 10 November 2026, no new open problem is inferred from the expository statement.

title: Rational decaying KP solutions and commuting pole dynamics
statement: Classify solutions of \(3u_{yy}+(4u_t+6uu_x+u_{xxx})_x=0\) rational in \(x\) and vanishing at infinity, through finite-dimensional commuting equations for their poles.
status: As of 10 November 2026, as of 10 November 2026, as of 10 November 2026, krichever\textquotesingle s 1978 Theorem 3 and corollaries solve the rational classification in its stated sense. Distinct-pole coordinates require local treatment across collisions, and the source\textquotesingle s particle coefficients must be normalized consistently. Earlier particle-integrability occurrences 1975-372.7 and 1975-372.12 are related background, not the same rational-KP question.

title: Inducing a unitary connection by orthogonal projection
statement: Given a smooth Hermitian vector bundle with a compatible connection over a finite-dimensional smooth manifold, realize it isometrically inside a finite-dimensional trivial Hermitian bundle so that its connection is the orthogonal projection of the trivial connection.
status: Affirmative before the seminar: the Narasimhan--Ramanan universal-connection theorem was announced in 1961 and is stated in the 1962 Prague proceedings. As of 10 November 2026, this is an established theorem, not an open problem.

title: Soliton resolution with the correct coherent structures and radiation
statement: In a specified class of global finite-energy sine-Gordon solutions, establish a large-time decomposition into finitely many localized coherent structures and radiation, with an explicit convergence topology; determine whether breathers and modified rather than free scattering are necessary.
status: As of 10 November 2026, Chen--Liu--Lu prove a precise generic weighted-Sobolev version with kinks, antikinks, breathers and modified radiation (preprint 2020, version 2022). The source\textquotesingle s unrestricted class and convergence topology are not fixed. Breathers are explicitly recognized in the notebook itself; no counterexample to that broader wording is claimed here.

title: Constructing a quantum inverse-scattering formalism
statement: For a specified classically integrable field equation, construct quantum scattering-data operators, their exchange algebra, commuting quantum integrals and eigenstates.
status: An early concrete solution is the Sklyanin--Faddeev announcement of 1978, especially its explicit nonlinear-Schrödinger construction. Its sine-Gordon comparison is expressly less complete. As of 10 November 2026, quantum inverse scattering is an established model-specific method; the notebook does not state a universal quantization theorem.

title: Describe projective bundles by finite exterior modules
statement: Can algebraic vector bundles on \(\mathbb P^n\) be represented and compared by graded modules of finite dimension over an exterior algebra? The notebook's broad classification question is indexed in the specific form answered by its theorem.
status: As of November 2026, the representation and stable-isomorphism criterion are established by BGG. A full explicit moduli classification is a different, substantially broader question and is not claimed solved here.

title: Why homogeneous functions define a line bundle
statement: Why do homogeneous rational functions of integer degree \(j\), regular above a projective open set, form a locally free sheaf of rank one?
status: Resolved classically: division by \(x_i^j\) gives an explicit local trivialization on \(x_i\ne0\). This is an exercise, not an open research question.

title: Cohomology of the integral formal substitution group
statement: Compute the cohomology of \(J=\{t+\sum_{i\ge1}a_it^{i+1}:a_i\in\mathbb Z\}\). The notebook leaves coefficients and topology unstated. This chapter distinguishes finite-jet cohomology \(\varinjlim_NH^*(J/(t^{N+1});A)\), continuous cochains, and unrestricted cohomology of the abstract group.
status: As of November 2026, Babenko--Bogatyi's real uniformly locally constant-support theory is computed and its continuous abelianization is known. For the explicit integral finite-jet refinement, the chapter derives torsion \((\mathbb Z/2)^2\) in degree two and a vanishing product of the two integral degree-one generators. It does not compute the full integral ring or the abstract discrete theory. Pavez-Cornejo's 2024 preprint/2025 publication uses closed commutators, not ordinary abstract commutators.
